narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and the assessment found an 84% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a high level of concern that ultimately led to the denial of your application. This decision was shaped by several aspects of your current financial profile, and understanding them may help you take meaningful steps forward.

The single most influential factor in this decision was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, only about 1 in 5 had a negative checking account balance, while the majority either had no checking account or maintained a positive balance. A negative balance signals to the assessment that your day-to-day finances may already be under strain, which raises serious questions about your ability to take on additional debt.

Closely related to this concern is the length of the loan you requested: 60 months, or five full years. This is dramatically longer than the average approved applicant, who typically requested credit over roughly 19 months. A longer loan duration means a longer period of financial commitment and exposure to risk, and combined with your already stretched checking account, this significantly amplified the concern about repayment.

The third important factor was your property situation, listed as unknown or no property. While this alone would not necessarily disqualify an applicant, it matters here because having no identifiable property means there is no financial safety net or collateral that could provide reassurance in case of repayment difficulties. Among approved applicants, nearly 9 in 10 had some form of property — real estate, a vehicle, or a savings-linked insurance plan — whereas only about 1 in 8 approved applicants shared your situation in this regard.

It is worth noting that some aspects of your profile are genuinely positive: your long employment history of seven or more years is a real strength, and owning your own home is also a favorable sign. However, these positives were not enough to outweigh the combination of a negative account balance, a very long requested loan duration, and the absence of property assets.

As a next step, you may want to consider applying for a smaller loan amount over a shorter repayment period, as this would substantially reduce the perceived risk. Working to bring your checking account into a positive balance before reapplying would also make a meaningful difference. Speaking directly with a bank advisor could help you identify the most realistic path toward a successful application given your circumstances.
